newsitem.title: NORWAY: Savings banks' bid for Fokus still stands.
newsitem.headline: Savings banks' bid for Fokus still stands.

text.p: Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 Norwegian savings banks, said on Friday its 73 crowns per share takeover bid for Fokus Bank still stands.
"If the bid is accepted, a possible cooperation agreement between Fokus Bank and Union Bank of Norway (UBN) would be dismantled," the group said in a statement to the Oslo Stock Exchange.
Fokus has recommended its shareholders to turn down the hostile takeover bid by Sparebankgruppen, which was made last month and is aimed at carving up Fokus among its members.

Fokus on Wednesday said it had held talks with UBN, known locally as Sparebanken NOR, on establishing a cooperation between the two banks. The cooperation would be based on both banks staying independent.
Fokus, UBN and Danish insurance company Codan Forsikring at the same time agreed on a similar cooperation in insurance. Fokus and Codan already work together in insurance matters in Norway.

Sparebankgruppen said it had told Codan and Norwegian agrarian bank Landkreditt, both of which are cooperating with Fokus, that it would offer to extend and expand cooperation with them should it acquire Fokus.
Sparebankgruppen said its goal remained to win acceptance for its bid by more than 90 percent of shares in Fokus.

"Because of the way things have developed we may agree to a lower level of acceptance than 90 percent because it would (still) provide a satisfactory basis for fulfilling the main strategic goals envisioned in the takeover bid," it said.
Fokus Bank, a commercial bank, is Norway's fourth biggest bank. UBN, a savings bank, is the third largest.
